card: Replaces time.time() with time.monotonic() when measuring durations in the functional test framework and HTTP test interface. Wall-clock time can jump or skew during test runs or under faketime, leading to flaky duration measurements and test failures. The author demonstrates reproducible test failures under faketime on feature_torcontrol.py and interface_http.py that this change resolves.
evidence: PR description: 'This helps preventing future clock jump flakiness (same class of bug as #36529) on tests and fix: faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.5" build/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py [and] faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.1" build/test/functional/interface_http.py'
problem: Functional test timeout and duration calculations using system wall-clock time (`time.time()`) can miscalculate elapsed time or fail if the clock jumps, adjustments occur, or when run under tools like `faketime`.

risk.why: Only touches Python functional test utilities and test harness code; a bug would only cause functional test failures.

summary: Replaces usages of `time.time()` with `time.monotonic()` for measuring time intervals across the Python functional test framework and test HTTP interface. This avoids duration calculation errors caused by system wall-clock adjustments or mocked time skews.
